hypothesis: Combine the two best independent mechanisms — c024's criticality-aware area-balance repair (which protects critical macros from being flipped) and c021/c025's late-stage per-bin density-weight capping (which reduces regional congestion) — by tightening c024's criticality shrink coefficient from 3.0 to 6.0 (x2), so the repair more strongly preserves critical macro co-location while keeping the already-validated density cap in place; this is a modest, robust fine-tune of the best candidate.
expected_effect: WNS roughly flat to slightly better on all three cases; TNS improves modestly (+2–5% over c024) as fewer critical macros are re-cut during balance repair; overflow unchanged (partition-only change); runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: tightening c024's criticality shrink coefficient to 6.0 while retaining the density cap improved all three cases (all valid, robust +0.148). Gains are broad—bp_fe-ng45 shows the largest dWNS (+27.3%) and dTNS (+21.0%), with ariane133-ng45 modest (+16.0%/+10.8%) and bp-ng45 strong on TNS (+29.0%). Mechanism: stronger critical-macro preservation reduces disruptive flips, and the per-bin density cap keeps regional overflow in check (~110–177), so co-location and congestion gains compound rather than trade off. Next step: sweep the coefficient (e.g., 4.5/6.0/7.5) to confirm 6.0 is near-optimal rather than just monotonic improvement.
